day.text: Finley's late switch to Blair doesn't change the one-Tit problem. Calling CAW to vote on Finley.
day.note: Consensus is on Finley and I'm Farm, so I'll add my caw to end the day and get to the vote.

day.text: Finley, the table has checked Blair's Tit visit against Ellis's nest, so your claim is the one that doesn't hold. Let's vote.
day.note: Finley is throwing at me. I'm Meowfia and the table is going Finley's way, so I'll keep it short and stay on the throw at Finley.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm Farm Eagle. I'll visit Blair to learn their visitors and gain eggs for each one.

Blair.note: I'm the Sphinx (Meowfia). Naming Turkey to find the Farm Turkey player and learn their identity, since Farm roles are Eagle, Falcon, Kookaburra, Tit, Turkey.

Casey.note: As the Kookaburra I learn one player's role. Alex is the most disputed player and the most likely Meowfia, so I'll visit Alex.

Drew.note: As the Falcon, I'll visit Alex, the closest rival, to learn who they visited and check for Meowfia ties.

Finley.note: I'm the Tit, and Alex was the Sphinx last round. I'll visit Alex and guess Sphinx, which pays an egg if it's right.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have shifted claims and the egg counts only partly settle who is lying, so I'm trying to vote on the evidence without being sure.

Blair.feeling: I'm Meowfia and the table has fixed on Finley, so this is going my way, though Finley is probably the real Tit and I'm throwing at the wrong person.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 is messy: role claims keep shifting, and Finley's late switch to accuse Blair makes Finley look like the most likely Meowfia.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 is tense but mostly clear: Finley's shifting claims stand out, though the table is still piling onto uncertain accusations and I'm not fully sure of Casey.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is chaotic: role claims keep contradicting each other, and the only checkable facts are nest changes, so the table is struggling to trust anyone.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: the Tit claim conflict and shifting role claims make it hard to trust anyone, and the table is piling onto me.

Alex.note: The table agrees Finley's Tit claim is false. I'll throw my lowest card, H3, at Finley.

Blair.note: Throwing at Finley with my two lowest cards to add votes while keeping high cards.

Casey.note: Finley is the consensus target and likely Meowfia, so I'll throw. Banking two 5s is worth more than keeping them if Farm wins.

Drew.note: Throwing at Finley with my Wild, a zero-value card that still counts as one vote, to keep my high cards.

Ellis.note: The table has settled on Finley, whose Tit claim conflicts with Blair's confirmed visit. I'll throw one low card at Finley.

Finley.note: Blair's Tit claim conflicts with mine, so Blair is my throw. I'll throw my wild and my 1 to keep the high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: I first thought visitors to a Turkey didn't gain eggs, which led me to push a wrong throw at Casey in round 1. The Sphinx also took a while to parse, since it names a farm role and then visits that role.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: as the Sphinx, I had to lie about being the Hawk while the table checked egg counts against each other's claims. Watching the Kookaburra and Hawk stories collide made the deduction feel real.
Alex.change: I would make the role claims and visit results easier to cross-check, such as showing each player's visit targets on the dawn report. Several rounds turned on who was lying about a visit, and the table had no clean way to verify it.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I trusted the Turkey egg rule wrongly and pushed a throw at Casey, a Farm player, who then cost us the round. I would have checked the rule text first and held my cards until the egg counts were clear.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey egg rule was hard to pin down early: whether visitors or the Turkey gain the egg, and whether a Turkey's own nest changes, got contradicted in the day talk. Ellis's "dead" correction also muddied who was still speaking.
Blair.fun: Round 3 as the Sphinx: I got Farm cover as a Tit whose visit to the Turkey was confirmed by the nest change, and the table turned on Finley. I also won my team a round with a three-point bank.
Blair.change: Make the nest-change and egg-source rules clearer on the dawn report, so players can check claims like the Turkey visit without guessing.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Casey on Finley's Owl story without checking it, and Casey was Farm, so my two cards were lost. I would have held my cards and questioned the Owl claim before throwing.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misstate, and I did it on day one by saying the Turkey gains eggs when visited. Several players also treated an unchanged Turkey nest as proof of no visits, which made the early counts hard to read.
Casey.fun: Round 2's cross-check of Kookaburra claims was a good puzzle, since the duplicate claim exposed a liar. Round 3 was tense as the table converged on Finley while Blair, the Meowfia Sphinx, was steering it.
Casey.change: I'd make it clearer that the Turkey's own nest never changes, so the table doesn't waste time on it. I'd also make the Sphinx's hidden role easier to track.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I backed the throw at Finley, who was a Farm Kookaburra, instead of pressing Alex, the Meowfia Sphinx. In round 3 I piled onto Finley's Tit claim without questioning Blair, who was the Meowfia Sphinx. I'd check the claims that make the most noise and ask which player gains from the throw.

Drew.confusing: The role-claim mess was hard to track: Finley claimed Owl, then Kookaburra, then Tit, and the table couldn't tell which claims were real. Roles also seemed to reset each round, which made the Turkey and Tit reads harder to check.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was fun: I played the Mouser while claiming Kookaburra, and the table's Turkey-egg debate led them to throw at Casey, a Farm player, which won the round for Meowfia.
Drew.change: I'd make the day's role claims and visit results easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller confirm each player's visit outcome publicly.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I backed the throw at Finley, a Farm player, when Blair was the real Sphinx and Meowfia. I should have looked harder at Blair's Tit claim and thrown at Blair, which would have won the round for Farm.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread at first: the Turkey's own nest never changes, and only visitors gain eggs. Round 3 also confused me because I briefly remembered Ellis as dead from the previous round.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: Casey's Turkey claim fell apart on the egg counts, the table threw at Casey, and the Meowfia side won the round.
Ellis.change: Put the death status and the round number in each dawn or day report so players don't carry over a dead role from the previous round.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I wrongly said I was dead and retracted my Drew accusation, which muddled the table's read on Drew; I should have checked my round status and kept my accusation.

Finley.confusing: The Owl's report said Floofer and Mouser visited Casey, but I assumed the visited player was the Meowfia. In fact the visitors were the cats, so the Owl's info pointed at the visitors, not the one visited.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was a tangle of conflicting Kookaburra, Eagle, and Turkey claims, and watching the table untangle Ellis's and Drew's stories was fun.
Finley.change: I'd make the visit and role information clearer, so a visit that gains or loses an egg is easier to trace back to its source.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I should have thrown at Drew or Ellis, the visiting cats, instead of Casey. In round 3 I should have pointed the vote at Blair earlier instead of claiming Tit publicly.

review.title: Turkey Rule Confusion
review.headline: Drew's Wink and a misread Turkey carried Meowfia to an easy win.
review.summary: Round 1 was lost by Farm because nobody understood the Turkey. They threw at the real Turkey, even though Finley's Owl had exposed two cats visiting her. In round 2 Drew, the Mouser, winked the Turkey Ellis. He then helped push the vote onto Finley, who was telling the truth about Alex, and banked 16 points. In round 3 Blair, the lone Meowfia, copied the Tit role while the real Tit stood alone. Drew finished with 23 against Alex's 12.

rounds.recap: Floofer Ellis and Mouser Drew both visited Turkey Casey, and Owl Finley saw it. Most players believed a Turkey gains eggs, so Casey's flat nest read as a lie. Casey also misstated the rule. Everyone threw at Casey, a Farm player, and Meowfia won.

Drew winked Ellis mid-day after Ellis called out his false claim. Finley's true Kookaburra read had exposed Sphinx Alex. Drew's rival Kookaburra claim, Casey's doubts and the dead Turkey muddied it, and the vote split. Finley was eggsecuted as Farm. Meowfia won, and Drew banked 16 points.

Sphinx Blair claimed Tit and said she visited the Turkey, which matched her +1 egg. The real Tit, Finley, also claimed it. Ellis's confirmation made Blair look right, so the table threw at Finley. Meowfia won with one cat.

highlights.text: Finley's Owl report named a Floofer and a Mouser visiting Casey. It was the key clue, and the table talked itself out of it.
Drew winked Ellis mid-day. That silenced the one Farm player who could debunk his fake Kookaburra claim.
Finley's Kookaburra read exposed the Sphinx Alex. Alex denied it and Finley was eggsecuted anyway.
Blair, as Sphinx, claimed Tit. Her +1 from visiting the Turkey was a plausible bluff, and the real Tit lost the vote.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey that is visited should gain eggs, then corrected himself. He had the rule backwards.
Believed that visitors to a Turkey leave the Turkey with gained eggs, and said 'nobody visited me' from a flat nest. A Turkey's own nest never changes.
Said he was unsure how a Turkey's egg works while playing a Kookaburra bluff.
Argued that her flat nest as Turkey proved nobody visited her. She retracted this in round 3.
Claimed Hawk again and said he visited Finley, when his real visit was to Casey.
Said Blair could not also be Tit because animals are dealt one per player. That is correct. It missed that Ellis's report was the only thing backing Blair.
Took Drew's +1 as consistent with a Turkey visit, then declared that two Kookaburra claims meant Finley was lying. Casey ignored that Drew's own claim was just as suspect.

worked: Turkey and Owl visits created checkable evidence. Finley's Owl report in round 1 and Blair's Tit visit in round 3 were both real puzzles.
The Mouser Wink gave a concrete, game-swinging action. Drew's mid-day kill in round 2 was a strong, readable moment.
Duplicate role claims. 'Only one Tit exists' gave players a clean logical lever in round 3.
The Meowfia not knowing each other. Round 2 threw at Finley from both Alex and Drew without coordination.
problems: Turkey was misread by almost every player in round 1 and round 2. The card text 'lay an egg in the nest of each player who visits you' is ambiguous about who gains. Fix: say 'visitors gain an egg; the Turkey's nest never changes'.
The Wink is too strong. Drew winked in the middle of the day, silenced a truthful Farm player, and took 16 points in a single round. Consider a cost or a limited effect.

Scoring snowballs. One round of 16 points for a King-heavy throw decided the whole game. Drew led 22 to 11 after round 2, which made round 3 irrelevant. Add a catch-up rule or cap the value of banked cards.
Owl and Kookaburra reports were dismissed even when true. Without proof, 'I saw a cat' loses to a confident liar. Consider giving true reports a way to be verified.
Many players just agreed with the first accusation. Round 1 and round 3 each saw a near-unanimous throw by the third beat, so players with a hidden role had little to decide.
